section.name: General
section.p: Please read general Migration Guide page first, for common considerations that apply to migration or upgrade between versions of Apache Tomcat.

section.name: Migrating from 8.0.x to 9.0.x
section.p: This section lists all the known changes between 8.0.x and 9.0.x which may cause backwards compatibility problems when upgrading.

subsection.name: Java 8 required
subsection.p: Apache Tomcat 9.0.x requires Java 8 or later. Apache Tomcat 8.0.x required Java 7.

subsection.name: Specification APIs
subsection.p: Apache Tomcat 9 supports the Java Servlet 4.0, JavaServer Pages 2.4, Java Unified Expression Language 3.1 and Java WebSocket 2.0 specifications. The changes between versions of specifications may be found in the Changes appendix in each of specification documents.

subsection.name: Servlet 4.0 API
subsection.p: In JSP pages that use wildcard import syntax the new classes added in Servlet API may conflict with ones in web applications. For example, if package "a" contains class PushBuilder, the following JSP page will cease to compile in Tomcat 8:

This happens because the implicit import of javax.servlet.http.* and the explicit import of a.* will provide conflicting definitions of class PushBuilder that was added in Servlet 4.0. The solution is to use the explicit import, import="a.PushBuilder".

subsection.name: JavaServer Pages 2.3
subsection.p: No information is currently available. It is anticipated that Java EE 8 will include a maintenance release of JSP with a version of 2.4.

subsection.name: Expression Language 3.1
subsection.p: No information is currently available. It is anticipated that Java EE 8 will include a maintenance release of expression language with a version of 3.1.

subsection.name: WebSocket 2.0
subsection.p: No information is currently available. It is anticipated that Java EE 8 will include an updated WebSocket specification with a version of 2.0.

subsection.name: BIO connector removed
subsection.p: The Java blocking IO implementation (BIO) for both HTTP and AJP has been removed. Users are recommended to switch to the Java non-blocking IO implementation (NIO).

subsection.name: Comet support removed
subsection.p: Comet support has been removed without a direct replacement. Applications using Comet are recommended to migrate to WebSockets.

subsection.name: TLS virtua hosting and multiple certificate support added
Internal APIs
subsection.p: Whilst the Tomcat 9 internal API is broadly compatible with Tomcat 8 there have been many changes at the detail level and they are not binary compatible. Developers of custom components that interact with Tomcat's internals should review the JavaDoc for the relevant API.

ul.li: Significant refactoring has taken place throughout the connectors to reduce duplicate code and to align behaviour across implementations.
